text: Git branching is a core part of version control, allowing multiple people to work on the same project without conflicts. Instead of everyone editing the main code directly, you create separate feature branches. Each branch is an independent copy of the project, where you can develop a new feature or fix a bug. Once your work is complete, the next step is merging. This combines your branch's changes back into the main branch. In many team workflows, you don't merge immediately. Instead, you open a pull request, which is a proposal to merge your code. Team members can then review your changes, discuss them, and approve them before the merge happens. This process keeps the main branch stable and ensures all code is checked and polished, making the whole version control workflow safer and more organized.
